water_supply_i.text: Urgent initiation of the watershed management projects through large-scale maintenance and repair of structures and artificial recharge especially in Jamnagar, Porbandar, Junagadh, Gir-Somnath, Botad, Dahod and Dangs which are mainly dependent on tanks, open wells, check dams and lift irrigation.

water_demand_i.text: Provide policy & price incentives for low water-guzzling crops such as millets (especially in the Eastern Tribal Belt), pulses, and spices.

Q1.label: High returns, high water demand
Q1.strategy: These are crops that have high returns which is the main deciding factor for the farmers, however, these crops are also having higher water demand. Therefore, demand-side management and reducing the crop water requirement through new varieties or practices such as mulching, micro-irrigation etc., may be promoted.

Q2.label: High returns, low water demand
Q2.strategy: These are crops that are ideal in terms of high returns as well as low water demand. Thus, such types of crops can be promoted in the respective regions.

Q3.label: Low returns, high water demand
Q3.strategy: These are crops that have low returns and high-water demand. Thus, there is a need for crop diversification or to undertake measures for getting higher returns along with reducing water demand.

Q4.label: Low returns, low water demand
Q4.strategy: These are the crops that have low returns and low water demand. From a water security perspective, they are preferable. However, to increase the return on these crops, there may be a need for market linkages and value addition for better price realization.

crop_caveat: The returns for various crops are taken from the APMC (2021). However, the high price fluctuation in Agri-commodities and therefore the returns may vary each year.

recommendations.label: What the study recommends
recommendations.formula: recommendations written for each region, from its aquifers, water balance, field survey and land use
recommendations.source: The study's region-specific water management strategies
limitations: Written for the region, not the district. Every district in a region carries the same three recommendations.
The study notes these strategies will need policy support to be carried out effectively.

atal_bhujal.label: Atal Bhujal Yojana
atal_bhujal.formula: the study's test for inclusion: a gap of more than 60% between demand and supply, with farming that leans on shallow groundwater
atal_bhujal.source: The study's recommendations on water supply
limitations: The scheme's coverage may have changed since the study was published.
The report names eight districts for inclusion. Aravalli, Devbhumi Dwarka and Morbi also pass its test; the study team has confirmed they should have been on the list.

crops.label: Crops by returns and water demand
crops.formula: each major crop's sales price and actual water use, classed high or low, place it in one of four groups
crops.source: Market prices from APMC, 2021, and water use from the study's household survey
limitations: Market prices change from year to year, so a crop can move between groups. The study notes this itself.
Grouped for the region, from the crops grown in its sample watershed. Every district in the region shows the same groups.
The printed table lists garlic twice for Saurashtra Hinterland; it is shown once, in the group the study's own calculation gives it.

named.label: Named in the study's recommendations
named.formula: recommendations the report makes for particular districts or a region
limitations: Quoted as the report words them.

contaminants.label: Found in groundwater
contaminants.formula: contaminants recorded in the district's groundwater: arsenic, fluoride, iron, salinity and nitrate
contaminants.source: The study's analysis of groundwater quality data, with INREM Foundation
limitations: Records which contaminants were found in the district, not how widely or at what concentration. A contaminant can affect a few villages or many.

This is why a district can carry several contaminants and still rate High for water and soil quality: the rating compares the share of the district affected with the state average, and covers salinity, fluoride and soil nitrogen, not arsenic or iron.
Fluoride and arsenic are health risks in drinking water as well as concerns for farming.

recommendations.demand_side: PGWM at different scales; adopting an ecosystem-based approach – attempt compensation for ecosystem services model in some areas

recommendations.supply_side: Protect and revive shallow aquifers and strategize efficient pumping of shallow aquifers; develop soil drainage and soil improvement programmes in areas prone to waterlogging and soil salinisation
recommendations.demand_side: Conjunctive use of surface water and groundwater through PIM and PGWM while ensuring crop water budgeting, especially over areas underlain by basalt aquifers; focus on ecosystem-based strategies

recommendations.supply_side: Improve efficiencies in pumping (reduce pumping rates) and long-term plans for reviving and restoring shallow aquifers that have either depleted or are saline
recommendations.demand_side: An aggressive, regional-scale PIM+PGWM campaign that combines efficient uses of groundwater and cropping pattern shifts – crop water budgeting based on large-scale groundwater balance estimates
